Title: HTTPS enforcement bypassed by a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto header
Description: The HTTPS check treated any request carrying the header X-Forwarded-Proto: https as secure, even when no reverse proxy is deployed. A client on plain HTTP could therefore submit credentials and receive a session token over an unencrypted connection.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Start APAS with the production configuration (no reverse proxy). 2. Send POST http://<host>/api/auth/login with a valid username/password and the header X-Forwarded-Proto: https. 3. Send GET http://<host>/dashboard with the same header.
Expected: POST rejected with HTTP 403 "HTTPS is required"; GET redirected to https:// with HTTP 301.
Actual: POST returned HTTP 200 with a session token over plain HTTP; GET was served (HTTP 302 to /login) instead of being redirected to HTTPS.

Title: Administrator overview dashboard exceeds the 3-second response target under concurrent load
Description: With 10 concurrent users, the 95th-percentile response time of the administrator overview dashboard (GET /api/dashboard as admin) was 4.19 s, with a maximum of 7.10 s. Overall p95 across all dashboards was 2.74 s, but one dashboard type broke the APAS-NF-001 target.
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Seed the test data plus 300 synthetic students (apas.seed.add_synthetic_students). 2. Run APAS over HTTPS and log in as admin, fac.rao and aarav. 3. Send 300 dashboard requests (6 dashboard types, 50 each) from 10 concurrent threads. 4. Compute the 95th percentile per dashboard type.
Expected: 95th percentile <= 3.0 s for every dashboard type.
Actual: admin API overview p95 = 4.189 s (max 7.102 s); faculty API overview p95 = 2.994 s (close to the limit).

Title: Risk and performance thresholds are not specified
Description: F-009 refers to 'configured thresholds' and F-014 to 'predefined risk criteria' without numeric values, so expected results cannot be derived from the SRS.
Steps to Reproduce: Review SRS v1.0, APAS-F-009 and APAS-F-014
Expected: Add default threshold values and state whether comparisons are strict (<) or inclusive (<=). Boundary tests TC-ANA-03.1 / TC-PRED-02.1 assume strict '<'.
Actual: Testers had to assume values: attendance < 75%, overall performance < 50%, failed subject < 40%; high risk = predicted SGPA < 5.0 or attendance < 65%; medium risk = predicted SGPA < 6.0 or attendance < 75%.

Requirement ID: SRS v1.0 sections 1.2 and 2.2 vs section 4 / RTM
Title: Assignment submission tracking has no functional requirement or test case
Description: Scope (1.2) and Major Product Functions (2.2) include 'Assignment submission and marks tracking', but no requirement from APAS-F-001 to F-015 and no RTM row covers it.
Steps to Reproduce: Review SRS v1.0 sections 1.2 and 2.2 vs section 4 / RTM
Expected: Either add a functional requirement (e.g. APAS-F-016) with acceptance criteria and a test case, or remove the function from the scope.
Actual: This function is untraceable and untested. The current build models only ISA/ESA assessments.

Title: 'Normal operating conditions' for the response-time target are not quantified
Description: The 3-second target has no defined concurrent-user count, data volume or network conditions.
Expected: Define the load profile (e.g. N concurrent users, M students, request mix) in the SRS or STP.
Actual: Cycle 1 assumed 10 concurrent users. Cycle 2 uses the team test-data profile TD-12 (50 concurrent users, 306 students), which is still not an SRS-approved figure.

Title: No acceptance criterion for prediction quality
Description: F-013 requires predictions to be 'generated and displayed' but sets no accuracy or error bound. The STP correctly forbids inventing one.
Steps to Reproduce: Review SRS v1.0 APAS-F-013, section 6; STP 15.1
Expected: Agree a target (e.g. MAE <= 0.5 SGPA on historical data) or record that prediction quality is informational only.
Actual: TC-PRED-01.4 can only report MAE/RMSE/precision/recall, not pass or fail on accuracy.

Title: RTM maps two different requirements to the same test case TC-SEC-01
Description: APAS-NF-003 (access restricted by role and permission) and APAS-SR-001 (valid credentials required) both map only to TC-SEC-01. NF-003 is about authorisation, which TC-SEC-02 covers.
Steps to Reproduce: Review SRS v1.0 section 8 RTM; STP 13.2
Expected: Map APAS-NF-003 to TC-SEC-01 and TC-SEC-02 (as done in the execution RTM).
Actual: Role-based restriction under NF-003 is not traceable to the RBAC test case.

Title: SRS allows plain HTTP, which contradicts APAS-SR-003
Description: Section 3.4 says communication 'shall use HTTP or HTTPS', while SR-003 requires HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and requires insecure connections to be rejected or redirected.
Steps to Reproduce: Review SRS v1.0 section 3.4 vs APAS-SR-003
Expected: State that HTTP is permitted only in local development environments without real student data.
Actual: Ambiguous whether HTTP is acceptable anywhere.

Title: Session timeout and account-lockout policy are not specified
Description: The SRS requires secure sessions but does not define an idle timeout or a brute-force lockout policy.
Expected: Add explicit values to the SRS security requirements.
Actual: The test build assumes a 30-minute idle timeout and a 15-minute lockout after 5 failed logins (TC-AUTH-03.3, TC-AUTH-01.6).

Title: Table text appears cut off in the SRS
Description: Text extracted from the 'Comments / Dependencies' column ends mid-word: 'Requires session mana' (F-003) and 'reporting servic' (F-012). This suggests the table cells overflow the page.
Expected: Check visually and widen or rewrap the table columns.
